title: Bypassing Copyright Protection in Diffusion-based Customization via Two-Stage Latent Feature Optimization

problem.claim: Copyright defenses for diffusion-based customization aim to prevent malicious content forgery in personalized image generation.

gap.claim: Existing defenses introduce persistent latent-space perturbations that remain susceptible to adaptive bypasses.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Two-Stage Latent Feature Optimization (TS-LFO), an attack for bypassing protected diffusion-based customization.
TS-LFO restores the disrupted mapping between input images and latent representations through two-stage optimization.
The method combines latent denoising with latent reconstruction to suppress defense noise and recover low-frequency semantic information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that TS-LFO consistently bypasses state-of-the-art copyright defenses.
The authors report that TS-LFO outperforms DiffPure, GrIDPure, and IMPRESS across diverse settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Copyright concerns have prompted adversarial defenses for diffusion-based customization.
Persistent latent perturbations used by current defenses can be adaptively bypassed.
TS-LFO restores the input-image-to-latent mapping through two-stage optimization.
Latent denoising improves alignment and suppresses high-frequency defense noise, while latent reconstruction recovers low-frequency semantic information.
The authors report broad bypass effectiveness and superiority to several prior attacks.

source_observation.claim: Defenses that disrupt input-to-latent mappings may be vulnerable to optimization that restores the mapping.

interpretation.claim: Robust protection should account for adaptive recovery of the representation pathway, not only persistent perturbation.

application.claim: Evaluate defenses against adaptive attacks that jointly optimize latent consistency and diffusion objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson generalizes beyond the reported diffusion-based customization settings.

unknowns: No datasets, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results are supplied.
The abstract does not specify the threat model, defense implementations, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess computational cost or reproducibility.
